newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE CHOICE BAD NEWS FOR CARLING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE CHOICE BAD NEWS FOR CARLING.

text.p: Phil de Glanville's selection as England's new rugby union captain is set to have an immediate knock-on effect for former skipper Will Carling.

The English team to face Italy at Twickenham on November 23 will be announced on Wednesday and De Glanville's confirmed place in the centre means Carling will face a real struggle to add to his 66 caps.
Coach Jack Rowell denied the appointment of De Glanville definitely spelt the end for Carling, but is likely to favour another Bath centre, Jeremy Guscott, in midfield against the Italians.
"We've had eight months to think about it, and there have been several outstanding candidates for the job," said Rowell, confirming De Glanville's appointment until the end of the season.
"It is a big challenge, but the new captain has already had success with the weight of expectation on his shoulders, and we are looking towards the next World Cup."
De Glanville, who has won 16 caps and occupied the replacements' bench 21 times, paid tribute to Carling's reign but sidestepped questions about his future role.
"Will thrust England into the forefront of world rugby, helped by a fantastic coaching set-up. But the time has now come for someone new to make a mark on the team.
"The team is not announced until tomorrow. I'm sure we will sit down and chat about it, but the selection is really down to Jack."

De Glanville has been injured for much of the last month, but has still been chosen ahead of prop Jason Leonard and flanker Lawrence Dallaglio as England's first formally-appointed captain since Carling's promotion in 1988.
"I am very pleased that Phil has been named captain, he is the right man for the job," said Guscott, who has been paired with Carling a world record 43 times.
"Phil has got the respect of all the international players, and has been knocking on the door for some time. It would be nice to play alongside him for England."
At 28, De Glanville's appointment is less dramatic than Carling's who was England's youngest skipper for 57 years when he took over aged 22.

But there are similarities between the two men, beyond their obvious shared playing position. Like Carling, De Glanville was educated at public school and attended Durham University in the mid 1980s where his ability was first recognised.
He played in the Varsity match for Oxford University before joining Bath, but has spent much of his subsequent international career shadowing Carling and Guscott.
As captain of the successful Bath club, he has earned considerable respect since recovering from an horrific eye injury sustained playing for the South West against the All Blacks in 1993.

Fifteen stitches were required to keep his eyelid intact after he was trapped at the bottom of a ruck, but he was fit and brave enough to share in England's victory over the tourists at Twickenham less than a month later.

Rowell believes he possesses both "tactical nous and leadership" and even Carling supported the decision. "I can congratulate Phil. I have always said that he is and will be an excellent captain," said the former captain.
"I appreciate the obvious ramifications for me, because there will be only one other centre choice beside the new captain. But it is now out of my hands, though I feel I am playing okay."
